Cognitive screening is largely preserved (MMSE 28/30). Routine labs and neurological exam are unremarkable, arguing against a metabolic, infectious, or primary systemic cause. The clinical picture fits the core features of behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD): early prominent disinhibition, apathy, loss of social decorum/empathy, and dietary/hyperoral changes with relative preservation of episodic memory and general cognition early in the course. Primary psychiatric disorders (e.g., mania, late‑onset psychosis) are less likely given the progressive course, age of onset, and prominence of hyperorality and social conduct changes. Neuroimaging (MRI or FDG‑PET) would be the next step to support the diagnosis by showing frontal and/or anterior temporal atrophy or hypometabolism.  
DIAGNOSIS: Behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD)
